Programming reference guides

Two separate guides, with matching topics and examples. Use Python to implement and test; use pseudocode to express and trace an algorithm clearly.

Pseudocode syntax and implementations

Choose your next step

  1. Begin with structure, variables, input and operators.
  2. Build decisions, loops, validation and reusable functions.
  3. Process lists, grids, dictionaries and files.
  4. Implement and trace searches, sorts, classes and inheritance.
  5. Use expected outputs, boundary cases and explained practice to check your work.

The two guides share stable topic anchors so you can switch language at the same topic. All answers are public learning support.

Downloads and offline use

  • Runnable Python examples (ZIP) — extract, then open README.txt; files are numbered by topic in this guide.
  • Pseudocode reference (Markdown) — plain text, including conventions and explained answers.
  • Complete offline library — both web guides and their downloads, keeping local navigation intact.

Use Print / save PDF in either guide for a full copy including answers. No account or specialist equipment is required.

Scope and sources

2026 foundation with 2027 revisions. Course-support examples complement the curriculum map; optional Python idioms are marked as extension. Pseudocode is an explicitly defined notation, informed by the SCSA support booklet, rather than an official compulsory grammar. The Python guide covers the programming strand used here, not every feature of the language.
